questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened to fill the tank, but when the tank is one-third full, a leak develops through which one-third of the water supplied by both pipes goes out. Find the total time (in hours) taken to fill the tank.
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened to fill the tank, but when the tank is one-third full, a leak develops through which one-third of the water supplied by both pipes goes out. Find the total time (in hours) taken to fill the tank.
questions.solution:
Let the total capacity of the tank is 100%.

The efficiency of the first pipe to fill the tank is 100/20 = 5% per hour

The efficiency of the second pipe to fill the tank is 100/30 = 3.33% per hour

The combined efficiency of both the pipes = 5% + 3.33% = 8.33%

Time taken by both the pipes to fill the one-third of the tank = 33.33/8.33 = 4 hours

Time taken by both the pipes to fill the whole tank = 100/8.33 = 12 hours

So, the total time (in hours) taken to fill the tank = 4 hours + 12 hours = 16 hours

.. The total time (in hours) taken to fill the tank is 16 hours.

Instead of: This phrase doesn’t fit with "prefer" because it suggests a substitution rather than a preference. It would be more appropriate in sentences like, "I drank tea instead of coffee."

1. For
Usage: To indicate a duration or a period of time.
Structure: "For" is followed by a time span (e.g., minutes, hours, days, months, years).
Examples:
"I’ve lived here for five years."
"She’s been studying for three hours."
"They have been friends for a long time."
Key point: "For" answers the question "how long?"
2. Since
Usage: To indicate the starting point of an action or state that continues up to the present.
Structure: "Since" is followed by a specific point in time (e.g., a specific date, day, time, event).
Examples:
"I’ve lived here since 2018."
"She’s been studying since 9 AM."
"They have been friends since college."
Key point: "Since" answers the question "when did it start?"
Quick Comparison
For = Duration (How long? e.g., for two hours)

questions.question: Which type of soil is not suitable for natural cultivation?
questions.questionHtml: Which type of soil is not suitable for natural cultivation?
questions.solution:
Laterite Soil is generally considered less suitable for natural cultivation. While it can support certain crops, its nutrient content is often low, and it can become hard and difficult to till, especially when dry.

It is also called Brick soil.

Other types of soils found in India: -

Alluvial Soil

 It covers about 40% of the total land area of the country and is widespread in northern plains and river valleys.

 Two different types of alluvial soils have developed in the Upper and Middle Ganga plains – Khadar and Bhangar.

o Khadar is the new alluvium and occupies the flood plains of the rivers. Khadar is enriched with fresh silt deposits every year.

o Bhangar is the old alluvium, deposited away from the flood plains.

Red soil

 It covers about 18.5 % of the total land area of the country.

 It is found in regions of low rainfall (eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau).

Black soil

 Black soil is also known as “Regur Soil”.

 It covers about 15% of the total land area of the country.

 It covers most of the Deccan Plateau – parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and some parts of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which of the following pair is/are correct? I. Prokaryotic cell – have single chromosome II. Eukaryotic cell – have more than one chromosome
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following pair is/are correct?
I. Prokaryotic cell – have single chromosome
II. Eukaryotic cell – have more than one chromosome
questions.solution:
Both statements are correct:

I. Prokaryotic cell – have a single chromosome: Prokaryotic cells typically contain a single circular chromosome located in the nucleoid region.

II. Eukaryotic cell – have more than one chromosome: Eukaryotic cells usually have multiple linear chromosomes housed within a nucleus.

In humans, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes. The 23rd pair is the sex chromosomes, while the first 22 pairs are called autosomes. Typically, biologically female individuals have two X chromosomes (XX) while those who are biologically male have one X and one Y chromosome (XY).
